instruction: Adversarial review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020F (Renovate shared preset + dependabot config) at safety/bypass lens. The preset is a supply-chain-critical artefact — it cascades to every adopter that extends it. Hunt for ways the preset could be exploited, weakened, or used to mask malicious changes. SPECIFIC ATTACK SURFACES: (1) Preset poisoning. Adopters extend the preset via `github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane//renovate/default#<tag>`. If the `renovate/v*` tag series can be force-pushed or re-pointed, an attacker who compromises the preset surface can push malicious updates to every adopter on their next Renovate run. The DISPATCH-NOTE acknowledges that `renovate/v*` is NOT covered by the 020J tag-protection ruleset (which targets `refs/tags/v*` only). Is this acceptable? Specifically: what happens if `renovate/v1.0.0` gets re-pointed at a malicious commit? The CODEOWNERS rule on `renovate/**` (from 020K) means the *file* requires @jrnb2024 review, but the *tag* is unprotected. (2) Wrapper marker escape. The customManager regex requires the canonical marker `# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=jrnb2024/standards-control-plane` AND the `uses:` line with `@<SHA>  # tag: <semver>`. Could a malicious adopter PR insert a *second* marker block pointing at a different repo (e.g., `attacker/malicious-fork`) and have Renovate happily bump that pin? Or use a homoglyph repo name (`jrnb2024/standards-control-plane‑` with a unicode dash) to mismatch Renovate's depName but pass GitHub's repo lookup? (3) Renovate `automerge: false` is set. But what if an adopter overrides `automerge: true` in their own renovate.json AFTER extending the preset? Renovate config inheritance is last-wins for some keys; verify the preset's automerge setting can't be silently overridden in a way that auto-merges malicious bumps. (4) The `extends: ["config:recommended", ":semanticCommits", ...]` — what does `config:recommended` actually pull in? Could a future Renovate-org change to `config:recommended` introduce automerge-by-default behaviour that this preset doesn't override? (5) `vulnerabilityAlerts.automerge: false` is set, but the schedule is `at any time` — could an adversary time a vulnerability disclosure to coincide with a CVE for an unrelated package and inject a bump under cover? (6) The Dependabot grouping: `gh-actions-minor-patch` groups all minor/patch bumps under one PR. If an adversary controls one of the bundled actions, a single PR bumps multiple actions; reviewer attention could miss the malicious one in the noise. Is there a recommended group-size cap or per-action review opt-out? (7) The dependabot config schedules on Monday 09:00 Europe/London — a predictable timing window. Not a vuln per se, but does it create an attacker-friendly preferred-disclosure-time pattern? (8) `prHourlyLimit: 4` on the Renovate preset: under a CVE storm, only 4 PRs/hour reach adopters. Could this throttle legitimate emergency bumps? (9) The preset's `prBodyNotes` includes a link to release notes — could that link be subverted (e.g., release notes editable post-publish to misrepresent what's in the bump)? (10) Renovate runs as Mend's hosted bot. Trust assumption is that Mend's infra is sound; the preset doesn't add a verification step (e.g., signature check on the bump PR). Acceptable for v1.0.0? Any bypass surface, weakening, or unintended consequence is a finding. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON.
